e-8161.problem:
Consider the the bilinear form $B(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}),$ given by 

$$
B(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})= 2 x_1y_2 - x_2y_2 +3 x_2y_3-x_3y_1
$$

 

Evaluate $B(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})$ when ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14043646/assets/dcea1a36972408a1f6a56577f61150bd8e4c2b91284820ca47c632a985d912ca.png) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14043646/assets/f9885ea740945a64e44931aca4befbd4022a84ae0fa1454627f2b44133eb4651.png)
e-8161.worked_solution:
We are given that 

$\qquad$ ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14043646/assets/652258046237288de7102e402a266dd3afff1abfecf97aa2156a351a7611afb3.png) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14043646/assets/58ef5fbadaf595035dc902aac9b66bbce61fea79b6a4144ed060f0486dda982c.png) 

Substituting these into the bilinear expression, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}B(x,y) & =2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}-{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{3}-{x}_{3}{y}_{1} \\  & =2\cdot 1\cdot 2-1\cdot 2+3\cdot 1\cdot 1-(-1)\cdot (-2) \\  & =4-2+3-2 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

e-8163.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix of a Bilinear Form
e-8163.problem:
The matrix of the bilinear form $B(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}) = 2x_1y_1 + 2x_2y_1 - x_3 y_2+2x_3y_3$ is given below. What is the value of $a+b+c?$

$$
[\begin{aligned}a & 0 & 0 \\ b & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & c & 2\end{aligned}]
$$
e-8163.worked_solution:
Each term $a_{ij}x_i y_j$ in the expression of the bilinear form corresponds to the entry $a_{ij}$ of the matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}B(x,y) & =2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{1}-{x}_{3}{y}_{2}+2{x}_{3}{y}_{3} \\  & =2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+0{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+0{x}_{1}{y}_{3} \\  & +\,2{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+0{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+0{x}_{2}{y}_{3} \\  & +\,0{x}_{3}{y}_{1}+(-1){x}_{3}{y}_{2}+2{x}_{3}{y}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, the corresponding matrix of the bilinear form is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14043646/assets/24b1e29dccdff51c2ca2c7780a8a5dfcf9c74ed91d48afdde8a14c5127f89ce1.png)

Therefore, $a=2,$ $b=2,$ and $c=-1.$ Finally, 

$$
a+b+c=2+2+(-1) = 3.
$$

after.problem: The linear form $f(x)$ is defined as $f(x)=ax,$ where $a=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}].$  Evaluate the function when $x=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: The linear form $f(x)$ is defined as $f(x)=ax,$ where $a=[\begin{aligned}6 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].$  Evaluate the function when $x=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 8 \\ -7\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:

after.name: Question 10
after.problem:
Consider the bilinear form $B(x,y),$ given by 

$$
B(x,y)={x}_{1}{y}_{1}+{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+{x}_{2}{y}_{2}.
$$

 

Evaluate $B(x,y)$ when $x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
We are given that 

$\,$ $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,y=[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

Substituting these into the bilinear expression, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}B(x,y) & ={x}_{1}{y}_{1}+{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+{x}_{2}{y}_{2} \\  & =1\cdot 3+1\cdot 3+2\cdot 1\cdot (-1)+1\cdot (-1) \\  & =3+3-2-1 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the bilinear form B(x,y), given by

B(x,y)=x1y1+x2y1+2x1y2+x2y2.

Evaluate B(x,y) when x=[11] and y=[3−1].

a

b
5
c
3
d
−4
e

Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We are given that

x=[x1x2]=[11] and y=[y1y2]=[3−1].

Substituting these into the bilinear expression, we obtain

B(x,y)=x1y1+x2y1+2x1y2+x2y2=1⋅3+1⋅3+2⋅1⋅(−1)+1⋅(−1)=3+3−2−1=3.

content.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Bilinear Form
content.problem:
Consider the bilinear form $B(x,y),$ given by 

$$
B(x,y)={x}_{1}{y}_{1}+{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+{x}_{2}{y}_{2}.
$$

 

Evaluate $B(x,y)$ when $x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
We are given that 

$\,$ $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,y=[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

Substituting these into the bilinear expression, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}B(x,y) & ={x}_{1}{y}_{1}+{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+{x}_{2}{y}_{2} \\  & =1\cdot 3+1\cdot 3+2\cdot 1\cdot (-1)+1\cdot (-1) \\  & =3+3-2-1 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 11
?

A=[2−331] Consider the matrix A above. Which of the following represents the corresponding bilinear form xTAy in terms of the components of x=[x1x2] and y=[y1y2]?

a
x1y1+3x1y2+3x2y1+x2y2
b
2x1y1+3x1y2−3x2y1+x2y2
c
x1y1+3x1y2−3x2y1+2x2y2
d
2x1y1−3x1y2+3x2y1+x2y2
e
x1y1−3x1y2+3x2y1+2x2y2
Submit

decision.explanation: Each matrix entry a_ij is the coefficient of x_i y_j. Thus x^T Ay=x_1(2y_1-3y_2)+x_2(3y_1+y_2), which expands to option d.

after.name: Question 11
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & \,\,-3 \\ \,\,3 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ above. Which of the following represents the corresponding bilinear form ${x}^{T}\,Ay$ in terms of the components of $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]?$
after.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

Each entry ${a}_{ij}$ of $A$ corresponds to the term ${a}_{ij}{x}_{i}{y}_{j}$ in the expression of the bilinear form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+(-3){x}_{1}{y}_{2}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+1{x}_{2}{y}_{2} \\  & =2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}-3{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

To write down a bilinear form in terms of vector components, we compute the following expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & \,\,-3 \\ \,\,3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2{y}_{1}-3{y}_{2} \\ 3{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={x}_{1}(2{y}_{1}-3{y}_{2})+{x}_{2}(3{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}) \\  & =2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}-3{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Writing Down a Bilinear Form Given Its Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & \,\,-3 \\ \,\,3 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ above. Which of the following represents the corresponding bilinear form ${x}^{T}\,Ay$ in terms of the components of $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]?$
content.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

Each entry ${a}_{ij}$ of $A$ corresponds to the term ${a}_{ij}{x}_{i}{y}_{j}$ in the expression of the bilinear form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+(-3){x}_{1}{y}_{2}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+1{x}_{2}{y}_{2} \\  & =2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}-3{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

To write down a bilinear form in terms of vector components, we compute the following expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & \,\,-3 \\ \,\,3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2{y}_{1}-3{y}_{2} \\ 3{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={x}_{1}(2{y}_{1}-3{y}_{2})+{x}_{2}(3{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}) \\  & =2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}-3{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 12
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ above. Which of the following represents the corresponding bilinear form ${x}^{T}\,Ay$ in terms of the components of $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]?$
after.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

Each entry ${a}_{ij}$ of $A$ corresponds to the term ${a}_{ij}{x}_{i}{y}_{j}$ in the expression of the bilinear form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =(-2){x}_{1}{y}_{1}+1{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+(-1){x}_{2}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2} \\  & =-2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+{x}_{1}{y}_{2}-{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

To write down a bilinear form in terms of vector components, we compute the following expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2{y}_{1}+{y}_{2} \\ -{y}_{1}+3{y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={x}_{1}(-2{y}_{1}+{y}_{2})+{x}_{2}(-{y}_{1}+3{y}_{2}) \\  & =-2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+{x}_{1}{y}_{2}-{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Method 1

Each entry aij of A corresponds to the term aijxiyj in the expression of the bilinear form:

content.knowledge_point: Writing Down a Bilinear Form Given Its Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ above. Which of the following represents the corresponding bilinear form ${x}^{T}\,Ay$ in terms of the components of $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]?$
content.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

Each entry ${a}_{ij}$ of $A$ corresponds to the term ${a}_{ij}{x}_{i}{y}_{j}$ in the expression of the bilinear form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =(-2){x}_{1}{y}_{1}+1{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+(-1){x}_{2}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2} \\  & =-2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+{x}_{1}{y}_{2}-{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

To write down a bilinear form in terms of vector components, we compute the following expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2{y}_{1}+{y}_{2} \\ -{y}_{1}+3{y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={x}_{1}(-2{y}_{1}+{y}_{2})+{x}_{2}(-{y}_{1}+3{y}_{2}) \\  & =-2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+{x}_{1}{y}_{2}-{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 13
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & \,\,-2 \\ \,\,-1 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ above. Which of the following represents the corresponding bilinear form ${x}^{T}\,Ay$ in terms of the components of $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]?$
after.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

Each entry ${a}_{ij}$ of $A$ corresponds to the term ${a}_{ij}{x}_{i}{y}_{j}$ in the expression of the bilinear form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =1{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+(-2){x}_{1}{y}_{2}+(-1){x}_{2}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2} \\  & ={x}_{1}{y}_{1}-2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}-{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

To write down a bilinear form in terms of vector components, we compute the following expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & \,\,-2 \\ \,\,-1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}-2{y}_{2} \\ -{y}_{1}+3{y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={x}_{1}({y}_{1}-2{y}_{2})+{x}_{2}(-{y}_{1}+3{y}_{2}) \\  & ={x}_{1}{y}_{1}-2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}-{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

b

c

x1y1−x1y2−3x2y1+2x2y2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Method 1

Each entry aij of A corresponds to the term aijxiyj in the expression of the bilinear form:

xTAy=1x1y1+(−2)x1y2+(−1)x2y1+3x2y2=x1y1−2x1y2−x2y1+3x2y2

Method 2

To write down a bilinear form in terms of vector components, we compute the following expression:

xTAy=[x1x2][1−2−13][y1y2]=[x1x2][y1−2y2−y1+3y2]=x1(y1−2y2)+x2(−y1+3y2)=x1y1−2x1y2−x2y1+3x2y2

content.knowledge_point: Writing Down a Bilinear Form Given Its Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & \,\,-2 \\ \,\,-1 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ above. Which of the following represents the corresponding bilinear form ${x}^{T}\,Ay$ in terms of the components of $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]?$
content.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

Each entry ${a}_{ij}$ of $A$ corresponds to the term ${a}_{ij}{x}_{i}{y}_{j}$ in the expression of the bilinear form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =1{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+(-2){x}_{1}{y}_{2}+(-1){x}_{2}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2} \\  & ={x}_{1}{y}_{1}-2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}-{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

To write down a bilinear form in terms of vector components, we compute the following expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & \,\,-2 \\ \,\,-1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}-2{y}_{2} \\ -{y}_{1}+3{y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={x}_{1}({y}_{1}-2{y}_{2})+{x}_{2}(-{y}_{1}+3{y}_{2}) \\  & ={x}_{1}{y}_{1}-2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}-{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 14
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ above. Which of the following represents the corresponding bilinear form ${x}^{T}\,Ay$ in terms of the components of $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]?$
after.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

Each entry ${a}_{ij}$ of $A$ corresponds to the term ${a}_{ij}{x}_{i}{y}_{j}$ in the expression of the bilinear form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+1{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{2} \\  & =2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

To write down a bilinear form in terms of vector components, we compute the following expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2{y}_{1}+3{y}_{2} \\ {y}_{1}+2{y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={x}_{1}(2{y}_{1}+3{y}_{2})+{x}_{2}({y}_{1}+2{y}_{2}) \\  & =2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

b
3x1y1+3x1y2−2x2y1+2x2y2
c
2x1y1+3x1y2+x2y1+2x2y2

Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Method 1

Each entry aij of A corresponds to the term aijxiyj in the expression of the bilinear form:

xTAy=2x1y1+3x1y2+1x2y1+2x2y2=2x1y1+3x1y2+x2y1+2x2y2

Method 2

To write down a bilinear form in terms of vector components, we compute the following expression:

xTAy=[x1x2][2312][y1y2]=[x1x2][2y1+3y2y1+2y2]=x1(2y1+3y2)+x2(y1+2y2)=2x1y1+3x1y2+x2y1+2x2y2

content.knowledge_point: Writing Down a Bilinear Form Given Its Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ above. Which of the following represents the corresponding bilinear form ${x}^{T}\,Ay$ in terms of the components of $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]?$
content.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

Each entry ${a}_{ij}$ of $A$ corresponds to the term ${a}_{ij}{x}_{i}{y}_{j}$ in the expression of the bilinear form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+1{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{2} \\  & =2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

To write down a bilinear form in terms of vector components, we compute the following expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2{y}_{1}+3{y}_{2} \\ {y}_{1}+2{y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={x}_{1}(2{y}_{1}+3{y}_{2})+{x}_{2}({y}_{1}+2{y}_{2}) \\  & =2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 15
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ above. Which of the following represents the corresponding bilinear form ${x}^{T}\,Ay$ in terms of the components of $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]?$
after.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

Each entry ${a}_{ij}$ of $A$ corresponds to the term ${a}_{ij}{x}_{i}{y}_{j}$ in the expression of the bilinear form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =(-2){x}_{1}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2} \\  & =-2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

To write down a bilinear form in terms of vector components, we compute the following expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2{y}_{1}+2{y}_{2} \\ 2{y}_{1}+3{y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={x}_{1}(-2{y}_{1}+2{y}_{2})+{x}_{2}(2{y}_{1}+3{y}_{2}) \\  & =-2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Method 1

Each entry aij of A corresponds to the term aijxiyj in the expression of the bilinear form:

xTAy=(−2)x1y1+2x1y2+2x2y1+3x2y2=−2x1y1+2x1y2+2x2y1+3x2y2

content.knowledge_point: Writing Down a Bilinear Form Given Its Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ above. Which of the following represents the corresponding bilinear form ${x}^{T}\,Ay$ in terms of the components of $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]?$
content.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

Each entry ${a}_{ij}$ of $A$ corresponds to the term ${a}_{ij}{x}_{i}{y}_{j}$ in the expression of the bilinear form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =(-2){x}_{1}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2} \\  & =-2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

To write down a bilinear form in terms of vector components, we compute the following expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2{y}_{1}+2{y}_{2} \\ 2{y}_{1}+3{y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={x}_{1}(-2{y}_{1}+2{y}_{2})+{x}_{2}(2{y}_{1}+3{y}_{2}) \\  & =-2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 16
after.problem:
$$
[\begin{aligned}6 & a \\ 0 & b\end{aligned}]
$$

The matrix of the bilinear form $B(x,y)=6{x}_{1}{y}_{1}-2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2}$ is given above. What is the value of $a+b?$
after.worked_solution:
Each term ${a}_{ij}{x}_{i}{y}_{j}$ in the expression of the bilinear form corresponds to the entry ${a}_{ij}$ of the matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}B(x,y) & =6{x}_{1}{y}_{1}-2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2} \\  & =6{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+(-2){x}_{1}{y}_{2} \\  & +\,0{x}_{2}{y}_{1}\,+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, the corresponding matrix of the bilinear form is

$$
[\begin{aligned}6 & -2 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, $a=-2$ and $b=3.$ Finally, 

$$
a+b=(-2)+3=1.
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix of a Bilinear Form
content.problem:
$$
[\begin{aligned}6 & a \\ 0 & b\end{aligned}]
$$

The matrix of the bilinear form $B(x,y)=6{x}_{1}{y}_{1}-2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2}$ is given above. What is the value of $a+b?$
content.worked_solution:
Each term ${a}_{ij}{x}_{i}{y}_{j}$ in the expression of the bilinear form corresponds to the entry ${a}_{ij}$ of the matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}B(x,y) & =6{x}_{1}{y}_{1}-2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2} \\  & =6{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+(-2){x}_{1}{y}_{2} \\  & +\,0{x}_{2}{y}_{1}\,+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, the corresponding matrix of the bilinear form is

$$
[\begin{aligned}6 & -2 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, $a=-2$ and $b=3.$ Finally, 

$$
a+b=(-2)+3=1.
$$

after.problem:
$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & b \\ a & \,\,-2\end{aligned}]
$$

The matrix of the bilinear form $B(x,y)={x}_{1}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{1}-2{x}_{2}{y}_{2}$ is given above. What is the value of $a-b?$
after.worked_solution:
Each term ${a}_{ij}{x}_{i}{y}_{j}$ in the expression of the bilinear form corresponds to the entry ${a}_{ij}$ of the matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}B(x,y) & ={x}_{1}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{1}-2{x}_{2}{y}_{2} \\  & =1{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{1}{y}_{2} \\  & +\,2{x}_{2}{y}_{1}\,\,+(-2){x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

    

Then, the corresponding matrix of the bilinear form is

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & \,\,-2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, $a=b=2.$ Finally,

$$
a-b=2-2=0.
$$

after.name: Question 18
after.problem:
$$
[\begin{aligned}a & b \\ -5 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

The matrix of the bilinear form $B(x,y)=-4{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{1}{y}_{2}-5{x}_{2}{y}_{1}-2{x}_{2}{y}_{2}$ is given above. What is the value of $a+b?$
after.worked_solution:
Each term ${a}_{ij}{x}_{i}{y}_{j}$ in the expression of the bilinear form corresponds to the entry ${a}_{ij}$ of the matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}B(x,y) & =-4{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{1}{y}_{2}-5{x}_{2}{y}_{1}-2{x}_{2}{y}_{2} \\  & =(-4){x}_{1}{y}_{1}+\,\,3{x}_{1}{y}_{2} \\  & +\,(-5){x}_{2}{y}_{1}\,+(-2){x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

   

Then, the corresponding matrix of the bilinear form is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-4 & 3 \\ -5 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, $a=-4$ and $b=3.$ Finally, 

$$
a+b=-4+3=-1.
$$

B(x,y)=x1y1+2x2y2+2x3y1+x3y2−3x3y3=1x1y1+0x1y2+0x1y3+0x2y1+2x2y2+0x2y3+2x3y1+1x3y2+(−3)x3y3

Then, the corresponding matrix of the bilinear form is

[10002021−3].

Therefore, a=1, b=2, and c=−3. Finally, a+b+c=1+2+(−3)=0.
